column1: # Star Fox (Switch 2, update v131072). In bring-up: see README.md

# A custom engine ("Viper": vfs, vrender, vjob, vscript, vspirv prefixes; Windows-built, project "eclipse"), SDK 21.4.4 built for the Switch 2 (Ounce), NVN2 with DLSS. Wwise 2024.1 audio, Bullet physics.
# Modules main, sdk, subsdk0 (movie), subsdk3 (nn::camera); subsdk1 (libc) and subsdk2 (NintendoSDK_DLSS) are not imported by main.
# The RomFS is one archive, data.zip: a zip with a VZIP preamble whose members are stored as 64 KB LZ4 chunks, each chained to the previous one (shader_split.py viper_zip_member).
# Packed from a NUP with scripts/pack_nup.py. Shaders: 2,828 NVN2 program binaries, one per member, in the engine's wrapper (shader_split.py viper_shader).
# Android: the game's DLSS (NVN2) runs on vka's stand-in, Snapdragon GSR2 3-pass (vka_dlss.c); the launcher's Upscaler row offers its modes, with Motion clarity
# (DM_VK_GSR2_CLARITY) and Temporal sharpness (DM_VK_DLSS_SHARP) sliders, in Game settings and the in-game panel
# The 3D scene (Game settings › 3D scene): the engine's own settings render.resolution_scale_console (0.5 on this console) and _handheld (0.833) as game arguments, which the
# engine reads before its settings file and keeps (README.md "The Picture"). Sizes at the phone's 1920x1080 output; dynamic resolution lowers them to 0.8 under load
# main imports nothing from subsdk1 (C / libc) or subsdk2 (NintendoSDK_DLSS) that the host does not supply (dm/games/profile_guess.py modules)
# The Switch 2's 9 GB. The NPDM declares 16 MB of system resource, so virtual address memory is on, and main never sets a heap.
# Measured through the prologue and the tutorial: the alias region mapped up to +8.26 GB of its 16 GB (8.5 GB resident, 4 GB GPU).
# On Android, phone RAM constraints require devices with 12 GB or 16 GB RAM; mem_map_limit is on by default.
# every shader is a member of /data.zip
